wv_eldorado_roofs.blurb: Eldorado Roofs is a small bouldering zone along Furnace Road in Coopers Rock State Forest, built around a pair of roofs in northern West Virginia. Ten problems are recorded, running from an easy V0 through the mid grades up to a few hard V6 to V8 lines, so the harder end is where most of the interest lies. The lines are long but low, so a few pads help. Holds in places are fragile, which makes it a spot to pick dry days for.

wv_giant_s_slab_boulder.blurb: Giant's Slab is a tall boulder in Darnell Hollow, part of Cheat Canyon's university forest in northern West Virginia, a short climb uphill from the last roadside pull-off. It is known for slab climbing on rock with plenty of small, distinctive features. Ten problems range from an easy V1 up to a V8, with a cluster of V6 and V7 lines at the top end and the best-liked ones sitting between V3 and V6. Expect to look up at it: the lines are tall, so bring pads.

wv_bear_haven.blurb: Bear Haven is a quiet rock outcrop and boulder cluster on a ridge of Shavers Mountain, roughly fourteen miles northeast of Elkins, set among hardwoods beside a small recreation area. Most of the ten recorded lines are boulder problems, mainly in the easy range from VB to V4, plus a few top-rope lines and one trad climb up to about 5.9. Spots for top-roping exist, but good anchors are scarce, so bring slings and webbing. It suits an unhurried visit rather than a big day of climbing.

wv_land_of_the_lost.blurb: Land of the Lost is the third and most remote of the three crags on Cotton Hill, down near the downstream end of the New River Gorge's climbing, lying beyond Cotton Club. It holds ten routes, a mix of sport and trad with one aid line, nearly all in the 5.10 range with a few at 5.11 and one 5.12, so it suits climbers comfortable on harder grades. The cliff gets sun early and shade later in the day. The hike up from the lot is a real uphill walk of around twenty minutes.
